Sync path: when any content block is untranslatable (thinking, redacted_thinking, server-tool, fallback), the whole native content list rides the response passthrough under 'content' and the Anthropic egress restores it 1:1 — Map.merge(built, provider_passthrough) already prefers it, so no egress change. Whole list rather than just the lost blocks because the reduction concatenates text, destroying boundaries. Carried only when something was lost, so ordinary responses don't record a false 'content dropped' for OpenAI-family clients. 5 new tests, 1101 pass. Streaming has the same hole and is filed separately as dodo_router-m9w.

DodoRouter.Logs.CacheRegression.classify/1 — pure, I/O-free, in KeyHealth.classify style. Takes a session's ordered logs, returns :healthy | :insufficient_data | {:regressed, finding} where finding names diverged_at, through, pinned_read, turns and uncached_growth.

Keyed on read-vs-input rather than the epic's stated cache_write growth: cache_write_tokens is NULL on 733/740 dev rows, so a write test would be blind (noted on the epic). Cuts the session into comparable runs first — same provider+model (caches are model-scoped) and gaps within the 1h TTL — then looks for a streak of >=3 consecutive turns that fail to read back more than the turn before, over >2048 tokens of new input. A read stuck at 0 counts only if the run cached earlier, so sessions with no caching at all stay silent.

12 unit tests including the AGENTS.md breakpoint signature, the collapse-to-zero case, and both token conventions. Verified against all 6 real dev sessions with 3+ logs: no false positives. Caveat: the dev DB holds no known-broken session to replay, so the positive case is the documented signature encoded as a fixture rather than captured logs.

Session list marks regressed sessions; the session view opens with a notice naming the diverging turn (linked, and the turn itself is ringed in the timeline), how many turns stalled, the pinned read, and how much input was re-sent at full price. A collapsible prefix diff shows the region both requests share — the part that was supposed to come back byte-identical — rendered with TextDiff at line granularity.

Logs.cache_verdicts/2 feeds the list: one query selecting only the six columns the classifier reads, so a page of 20 sessions does not load 20 sessions' worth of bodies. 5 new LiveView tests, 1118 pass.

Both children shipped. A session whose cached prefix stops hitting is now detected by Logs.CacheRegression and surfaced in the session list and view, naming the diverging turn and diffing the shared prefix.

One gap against the epic's original acceptance criteria, worth knowing: the operator is alerted where they already look, but nothing pushes at them — they still have to open the sessions page. Pushing anomalies is dodo_router-ajp.3 (Attention panel), which this now feeds.

All three streaming controllers now pass request_id: into dispatch_streaming, so the x-request-id the client was handed is the request_id on the log row. Four integration tests over the real HTTP path: one per streaming endpoint (OpenAI, Anthropic, Responses) plus sync as a regression guard — all three streaming ones failed before the fix, sync passed. 1122 tests.

Adapter.record_stream_response_headers/1 lets a streaming adapter park the provider's response headers the moment the upstream head arrives — before the first chunk, the last point the egress head is still revisable. AnthropicProxyController.open_stream applies the anthropic-ratelimit-* ones there, matching what the sync path does from the dispatch meta. Reset per request since keep-alive reuses the process.

Wired into Adapters.Anthropic (real path) and TestProvider (so the whole path is testable end to end). Two integration tests over the real HTTP path, sync and streaming; both failed before. There was no coverage for the sync forwarding dor.4 landed either — now there is. 1124 tests. AGENTS.md documents the seam alongside the other streaming-egress rules.

Replays.replay now decodes the root log's stored request_headers and passes them as client_headers, so a replay reaches the provider carrying what the original traffic carried. Anything holding the redaction marker is dropped — the stored credential is a marker, not a secret, and the replay authenticates with the router's own key; everything else goes through Adapter.build_forwarded_headers/2, the same policy live traffic passes through. Evaluation candidates go through Replays.replay, so they inherit the fix.

Deliberately NOT extended to the eval judge: that is a synthetic judging prompt, not a stand-in for the original request, so forwarding the user's anthropic-beta (or anything else) onto it would be arbitrary rather than faithful. 2 tests, 1126 pass.

Adapter.record_outbound_body/1 records the built body and returns the payload size — folded into the one line every adapter already had (payload_size_bytes = body |> Jason.encode!() |> byte_size()), so all 8 request-making adapters were migrated by replacing that idiom rather than by adding a call each could forget. FallbackChain resets before each step and harvests after, alongside Fidelity.take/0; an adapter returning outbound_body in its own meta still wins, so ResponsesAPI is unchanged. Size is handled by the existing Proxy.maybe_truncate_step_field/2.

adapter_header_coverage_test.exs now also sweeps for it: any adapter whose source calls Req.* must record. Delegating adapters (Groq, Mistral, xAI, DeepSeek, Codex) are exempt by construction rather than by a hand-kept list, since the module they delegate to is swept on its own. Plus an end-to-end test that the bytes reach attempted_steps. 1128 tests. AGENTS.md table row updated.

Both directions. Request: ResponsesFormat.passthrough_fields/1 plus client_format: :responses from the controller, and Adapters.ResponsesAPI merges the untranslated fields under the body it built — same shape as the Anthropic path, and the machinery was already format-agnostic so nothing in FallbackChain changed.

Response: the response.completed event's own object minus what the conversion consumed rides Adapter.response_passthrough_key/0 from the SSE accumulator, and from_openai_response/3 merges it over the synthesised response. That egress hardcodes instructions/temperature/previous_response_id/text.format to nil, so the passthrough is what stops those being lies — and it restores the provider's real resp_... id, which is what a client needs to chain the next turn via previous_response_id.

Turned out to be cheap, because the bead's premise was off: the real msg_ id is not a tail field. Anthropic sends it in message_start, before any content_block_delta — so it is already in hand when the egress opens its own stream, with no time-to-first-byte cost and no change to the 'defer send_chunked until the first chunk' rule.

The accumulator now keeps message_id, Adapters.Anthropic.stream_message_id/0 exposes it, and open_stream uses it or synthesises one when a non-Anthropic provider served the request. One ordering fix came with it: the accumulator is parked in the process key before chunks are forwarded rather than after, so a frame carrying message_start and a delta together cannot hand the egress a stale accumulator. 2 tests, 1138 pass. AGENTS.md's 'cannot be back-filled' note corrected.
